A1: For twenty years, risk models were built in R. A statistician writes the script, runs it on their own laptop, and emails the numbers. It works, until that person leaves.
A2: R runs in memory, one thread at a time, and it's hard to plug into production. Meanwhile, fifty-eight percent of developers use Python. R? Five.
A3: So why R, and not SAS? SAS migration is already industrialised: EXL's own Code Harbor cut conversion time by seventy percent. R is the gap: twenty-two thousand open packages, each with its own defaults.
A4: And those defaults are the trap. Under PRA SS1/23, a rewrite is a model change that needs evidence. One hidden penalty or missing-value rule, and a coefficient shifts enough to flip a loan decision.
A5: Meet R-Pythonizer: a web platform that moves statistical models from R to Python, and proves the result. The rule is simple. AI writes the Python. Plain code proves it. A human approves. And if a model has no faithful Python equivalent, the platform says so and stops.
A6: R runs the model once and freezes an answer key. Python gets R's exact rows, and the AI never sees R's numbers, so it can't cheat. Then plain code checks every coefficient and prediction, and if anything fails, an agent finds out why.
A7: But a perfect copy of a bad model is still a bad model, so we also check calibration, stability and fairness, as a separate verdict.
A8: Seven fixed steps, four narrow agents, zero data rows, and a script anyone can re-run. We tried four AI models, and GPT-6.1 terra, fast and cheap, got the same verified result for under five cents.
B1: Let's try it on a real credit-default model: an R notebook and a hundred and fifty thousand rows.
B2: The Analyst agent drafts the spec, and even flags what's missing, like a labelled holdout set.
B3: R runs once and freezes the answer key.
B4: The Translator writes Python, and twenty-five checks pass: coefficients and predictions match R to thirteen decimal places. Business fitness? Not established yet, and the platform tells you exactly why.
B5: The report backs every number with evidence, and the package re-runs the proof anywhere.
B6: R-Pythonizer. AI writes, code proves, humans approve.
